h1: My biostimulant's provisional registration ended in June 2025. What can I do now?
title: Biostimulant provisional registration ended: what now? | GBO
desc: Your G3 lapsed in June 2025. What official text says on listed products and new data, and the old stock question it leaves open.
answer: Your G3 certificate has stood invalid since 17 June 2025, with no further extension. The official route onto the list runs through data on bioefficacy, toxicity and chemistry. Otherwise, look at products already in Schedule VI. The release is silent on old stock, so check with your state agriculture department before moving any.
sections:
The Ministry of Agriculture and Farmers Welfare set out the position in a release of 9 September 2025. Provisional certificates (G3) went to more than 8,000 products. The last extension ran to 16 June 2025. The government decided "not to give any further extension". The release says provisional registrations "stand invalid since 17.06.2025".

So your first job is a records job. The release says a list of the invalid provisional registrations is on the Department of Agriculture website, under Documents, Circulars/Notifications, Biostimulants. Find your product and certificate there. Keep a dated copy.

The release counted 146 products in Schedule VI as of September 2025. That is the latest official count we could open for this guide. It may have changed, so read the latest Gazette list on the same Department page. A release of 15 July 2025 said the number had come down to "approximately 650". It does not say what was counted and does not mention Schedule VI. Do not use it as the listed count.

A note on our reading. We could open the two PIB releases, the state pages and the court judgment linked here. The Gazette PDFs and the Department page would not open for us, so this guide quotes no clause of the Order on biostimulants. Read those notifications yourself, and check with your state agriculture department.
Your options against the official text

OptionWhat the release saysWhat it does not sayYour next step
Wait for another extensionNo further extension beyond 16 June 2025.Whether any relief could come later.Do not plan around one.
Move to a product already in Schedule VI146 products were included as of September 2025, through Gazette notifications.How a brand moves, who may use an entry, or how close a formula must be.Compare your label with the Gazette entry, then ask your state.
Apply with dataData on bioefficacy, toxicity and chemistry is a prerequisite for inclusion.Forms, fees, laboratories or timelines.Get the current procedure in writing before you fund a trial.
Deal with old stockNothing specific.Whether stock may be sold, returned, relabelled or destroyed.Hold it and ask your state in writing.

This table is a reading of one release, not legal advice. Check with your state agriculture department.
Moving to a product already listed

Schedule VI sits in the Gazette notifications, and the release groups it into nine categories, (a) to (i). They run from botanical extracts, including seaweed extracts, to humic and fulvic acids and live micro-organisms. Read the Gazette entry itself, not a summary of it.

The limit is plain. The release does not explain how a brand moves from a lapsed product to a listed one. It does not say whether a listed entry can be used by a company other than the one that generated its data. It does not say how close a formula must be. Do not assume that a similar name or a similar active is enough.

A practical way to work:

  • Put your old label beside the Gazette entry. Compare material, source, concentration and form.
  • Treat any mismatch as a different product until an official tells you otherwise.
  • Do not carry old label claims across without checking them against the new product.

Your state file may need a fresh look too. Bihar's online checklist for a no-objection certificate to sell biostimulant products lists the G-3 certificate as a required document. The page carries no date. It shows how a state file can rest on the G3. If yours does, ask what your state now accepts. Check with your state agriculture department.

The release is clear on one point. The provisional period was meant to give manufacturers and importers time for "generating data on bioefficacy, toxicity, chemistry, etc." It calls that data a prerequisite for inclusion in Schedule VI.

Note who it names: manufacturers and importers. If you only marketed the product under your brand, first find out whose name was on the G3 and who holds any data. If no data was generated, there is nothing to file yet.

The July 2025 release points the same way. It quotes the Union Agriculture Minister: "Biostimulants will only be approved if scientifically validated". He also said ICAR must test effectiveness, and that clear rules and SOPs must be established. The release does not say whether those rules have since been issued, so look for them on the Department page.

The September release gives no form, fee, laboratory or timeline. It mentions no grace period for a product whose data is still being prepared. We will not fill those gaps with a guess. Ask these before you spend on trials:

One court order is worth knowing. A Delhi High Court judgment of 18 August 2025 allowed firms whose Schedule VI applications were pending, or had deficiencies pointed out, to operate until a decision on those applications. That benefit was limited to members of the petitioner associations and the other named petitioners. It is not a general extension, and rejected applicants did not get it. Our guide to the FCO forms explains more. Check with your state agriculture department.

  • Which notification sets the current procedure?
  • Who must apply: the brand owner, the manufacturer or the importer?
  • Which tests are accepted, and where must they be done?
  • Can the product be sold at all while the file is under review?

Read the Department's notifications, and check with your state agriculture department.
Old stock: the official text is silent

The September release says the extensions let existing manufacturers and importers make or import for sale, sell, offer for sale, stock and exhibit biostimulants for a limited period. It then ends the extensions. It says nothing specific about packs already made, in your warehouse or on a dealer's shelf.

So we will not tell you that old stock may be sold, returned, relabelled or destroyed. The release does not say, and a trade rumour is not a rule.

One trap to avoid. An older copy of the Fertiliser (Control) Order on an Odisha government site has clause 31. It says a dealer or certificate holder "may be allowed for a period of thirty days" to dispose of balance stock, when debarred or when a certificate is cancelled. The word biostimulant does not appear in that copy. Do not read it as permission for stock under a lapsed G3.

Until you have an answer:

  • List every batch with quantity, location, manufacture date and G3 number.
  • Include stock already with dealers and distributors.
  • Do not move, discount or relabel it on your own reading.
  • Ask in writing and keep the reply.

This is a state-level question for your own facts. Check with your state agriculture department.
What we can say from our side

We can speak only for our own position. We hold Gujarat NOCs for 36 FCO Schedule VI biostimulant grades and 11 biofertiliser types. We make them at our own plant at GIDC Shihor, Bhavnagar, with 100 KL liquid and 2,500 t solid a month. We have worked with farmers since 2006. Our seaweed and humic are extracted in-house by a mild process, without harsh chemicals, very high pH or heat.

If the listed route suits you, compare your old label with that grade list and with the Gazette entry. Our NOCs are Gujarat documents for our grades. They do not revive a lapsed product, and they do not settle what your state requires of you. Check with your state agriculture department.

The private label and state partner programme pages explain how we work with marketers. We promise no brand under either.
faq: Is my G3 certificate still valid?
The PIB release of 9 September 2025 says provisional registrations stand invalid since 17 June 2025, and that no further extension would be given. Check with your state agriculture department.
How many biostimulants are in Schedule VI now?
The release counted 146 as of September 2025. That is the latest official count we could open. It may have changed, so read the latest Gazette list.
Can I sell the old stock I still hold?
The official release is silent on old stock, and we will not guess. Hold it, list it by batch and check with your state agriculture department.
Can I keep selling while I generate data?

The release mentions no grace period for a product whose data is still being prepared. A Delhi High Court judgment of August 2025 gave limited relief to named petitioners only. Check with your state agriculture department before any sale.
What data is needed for Schedule VI?
The release names data on bioefficacy, toxicity and chemistry, among others, as a prerequisite. It gives no forms, fees or timelines, so get the current procedure from the Department's notifications.
Does the state partner programme come with a brand?
No brand is promised. The programme page explains how we work with marketers.
